title: Welcome to the Old Testament

footnotes.text: Malachi, the author of the final book in the Old Testament, wrote and prophesied in approximately 430 BC (see Bible Chronology, “Chronology of the Old Testament”; Guide to the Scriptures, “Malachi,” Gospel Library).

See Bible Dictionary, “Bible”; Richard Neitzel Holzapfel and others,Jehovah and the World of the Old Testament: An Illustrated Reference for Latter-day Saints(2009), 374; M. Russell Ballard, “How the Lord Prepared the World for the Restoration,”EnsignorLiahona, Jan. 2020, 16.
See Bible Dictionary, “Bible.”

See Holzapfel and others,Jehovah and the World of the Old Testament, 374. The Dead Sea Scrolls, which were discovered beginning in 1947, are a collection of numerous ancient manuscripts and fragments that contain some of the oldest samples of Old Testament texts in Hebrew.
See Bible Dictionary, “Septuagint.”

See Michael D. Coogan and others, eds.,The New Oxford Annotated Bible: New Revised Standard Version, 5th ed. (2018), 1845; see also Holzapfel and others,Jehovah and the World of the Old Testament, 374. With the discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls beginning in 1947, scholars found that the texts of the Dead Sea Scrolls—which were more than a thousand years older than the Masoretic text—closely matched the Hebrew texts preserved by the Masoretes (see Holzapfel and others,Jehovah and the World of the Old Testament, 374–75).
See Bible Dictionary, “Bible.”
See the section titled “Lost Scriptures” in Guide to the Scriptures, “Scriptures,” Gospel Library.

See Guide to the Scriptures, “Bible,” Gospel Library. When Jesus spoke about the Law and the Prophets (seeMatthew 7:12;22:37–40), He was referencing this structure of the scriptures.
These five books are also called the Torah (Hebrew for “teachings”) and the Pentateuch (see Guide to the Scriptures, “Pentateuch,” Gospel Library).
Joseph Smith noted that the Song of Solomon is not an inspired book (see Bible Dictionary, “Song of Solomon”).
